glass.readme:
Hover a link and its note shows in a post-it on the glass, above every screen (PIE-1481; an extension since PIE-1505).

- **Turn it on:** click ◇ on the status bar, or alt+u: off → on → sticky → off.
  - **on:** a post-it opens once the pointer rests on a link, a cut-off title or a note row, and closes after it leaves.
  - **sticky:** each hover stays as a post-it until you dismiss it.
  - alt-hover keeps one sticky, even with hover off.
- **In a post-it:** ← → flip through what you hovered before (the wheel over its title too).
  - p keeps it (◇ ◆ on its title), alt+E peels the shown note into its own post-it, alt+X drops it from the stack.
  - Esc dismisses it; alt+U, or an alt-click on ◇, clears the glass.
- **Shelves:** `glass.shelf name=seeds colour=amber` makes a named, coloured shelf; drag post-its onto it, or `glass.shelve ref=<id> shelf=seeds`.
  - v switches it between a list and a grid, c its colour.
- **Delays and limits:** Tune → Glass (G): open, close and grace delays, the hover history's length, the pinned soft limit. `glass.tune name=open value=150` from anywhere.
- **On by default:** a default-on built-in (`defaultOn`): the host installs it at start wherever it runs, unless you uninstalled it there.
- **Remove:** `ep0ch act extensions.uninstall id=glass demo=keep`.
  - Hover then does nothing and ◇ is gone; `glass.*` says how to bring it back: `ep0ch act extensions.install id=glass`.
  - The glass itself stays: `tile.float to=glass` (^W U) still keeps any tile above every screen.

waiting.readme:
Waiting on others: every outbox item still waiting for an answer, grouped by who it waits on, the longest wait first (the door's built-in screen until PIE-1525; an extension since).

- **Open it:** O on the main menu, `ep0ch --screen waiting`, or `act screen.open name=waiting`.
  - The list sits beside a reader; j k pick a row and the reader shows it (the list's select wire).
  - ⏎ opens the item where opens land; / filters the rows.
  - `act tile.open kind=waiting.list` opens the list as a tile anywhere (it takes no `^W o` key: O is never one, and W is What changed's).
- **What waits:** a note with `[type::outbox-item]` and `[outbox::waiting]`.
  - `[waiting-on::Ada: which shelf do the jars go on?]`: the name before the colon is the group, the rest the question; without it, `[to::…]` and the title.
  - `[sent::2026-01-05 4:23 PM]` (a date as people write it) is when the wait began; without it, when the note was written.
  - A wait past three days is drawn as a warning; `warn-days` in its settings says another number (the bar's Extensions, "Settings of Waiting", or `act extensions.configure id=waiting warn-days=7`).
- **In a note:** a `waiting::` line draws the same list there.
- **On by default:** a default-on built-in (`defaultOn` in its manifest): the host installs it at start wherever it runs, unless you uninstalled it there.
- **Remove:** the extensions screen's row (ctrl+k, then `&`), or `ep0ch act extensions.uninstall id=waiting demo=keep`.
  - The main menu's O row and the waiting screen go with it; `ep0ch --screen waiting` then says how to bring it back.
  - It stays off until `ep0ch act extensions.install id=waiting`, which brings both back with no restart.

- A tile: **What changed** (`what-changed.list`): the notes others changed since you last looked (who, what, when), newest first; ⏎ opens one where opens land, alt+⏎ in a new detail, d the change beside it, / filters
what-changed.readme:
The notes others changed since you last looked, as a tile the service draws (PIE-647; an extension since PIE-1506).

- **Open it:** alt+o on any screen, or a click on the status bar's `+N new`: the list comes up in your drawer, and looking marks what it holds seen.
  - The door keeps the count and your seen position; this extension draws the rows.
  - `^W o W` opens one on the desk, `act tile.open kind=what-changed.list` too (`with='{"since":"2026-11-01T00:00:00Z"}'` lists from a time).
- **In it:** j k pick a row, and the preview follows.
  - ⏎ opens the note where opens land; alt+⏎ opens it in a new detail.
  - d shows the change beside the note, in the reader's revision compare (← → older and newer, Esc back).
  - / filters the rows.
  - Rows you haven't looked at wear ●.
  - Your own edits are never listed.
  - Tools' bookkeeping and extensions' writes are held back until the menu's `changes.machinery` shows them.
- **In a note:** `what-changed:: since=2026-11-01T00:00:00Z` draws the same list there.
- **On by default:** a default-on built-in (`defaultOn` in its manifest): the host installs it at start wherever it runs, unless you uninstalled it there.
- **Remove:** `ep0ch act extensions.uninstall id=what-changed demo=keep`.
  - It stays off until `ep0ch act extensions.install id=what-changed`.
  - Meanwhile alt+o shows the tab saying its kind is gone, and `+N new` still counts.

- Rule `settle`: runs settle on start, settle on change, agent on from. Asks the write review about a note an agent wrote, a minute after it was last saved, and marks what it finds
```text

query: NOT type=annotation NOT type=annotation-reply NOT type=peer-message NOT type=draft-proposal NOT type=snapshot NOT type=virtual-branch NOT type=jev-run NOT type=review-finding NOT machine NOT demo NOT from NOT ext.page NOT asks=off NOT type=permission-ask NOT type=proof NOT type=implementation-proof NOT type=validated NOT type=landed NOT type=merge NOT type=decision NOT type=build-log NOT type=log-entry NOT type=release-notes NOT type=artifact-run

- Rule `clear`: when a note matches query `asks.derived`, propertyScope `all`, runs clear on change, clear on stop. Takes a mark off when its line is ticked, you reply under it, or the note reaches done
- Rule `reply`: when a note matches query `type=annotation OR type=annotation-reply`, runs reply on start, user on from. Takes a mark off when you comment on its line, or on the whole note
- **Settings,** once it's installed: ⚙ settings on its page, or `ep0ch act ext.asks.settings <field>=<value>`:
